label: verify-t6-flyingfish-deep

claims.claim: Stuffed Cypselurus hiraii models in a 12 m/s tunnel (Re ~2e4) reach L/D at most 4.37 and CL at most 0.78; this is the only direct force measurement on flying-fish bodies and underlies every range bound.
claims.source_says: Flying fish (Cypselurus hiraii) AR 10.7, L/DMAX 4.37 (0), CL,MAX 0.78 (35), CD,MIN 0.055; "free-stream velocity (u) of 12 m s-1"; models were stuffed fish; "detailed measurement of wing performance ... has not been performed yet".
claims.note: Numbers and 12 m/s match the Park and Choi PDF; 'only direct' and 'underlies every bound' are the agent's framing, but the paper itself says no prior force measurement existed.

claims.claim: Deng 2019 headline (45.4 m, 13.2 m apex) rests on a fixed 20 m/s take-off, coefficients computed at 10 m/s, and pairs a 0-degree distance with a 10-degree apex (whose best distance is 41.5 m).
claims.source_says: "The take-off speed is fixed at 20 m s-1 for all the calculations"; alpha0=10: "distance ... 41.5 m ... maximum height of 13.2 m"; "a fixed velocity of 10 m s-1 is considered ... for the aerodynamic coefficients".
claims.note: All three parts confirmed in the Deng text; the 0-degree run gives 45.4 m with a 12.5 m height, so the conclusion pairs numbers from different runs.

claims.claim: Aquarium Cypselurus heterurus doederleini leaped at an estimated 3.9-5.2 m/s, well below the derived 9.85 m/s stall speed for L3; quoted field values (leap 10 m/s, glide 50 m, air speed 15-20 m/s) are second-hand from older film work.
claims.source_says: "the flying fish were estimated to leap from the water surface at speeds of 3.9 to 5.2 m s-1"; intro: stroboscopic filming (Edgerton & Breder 1941, Davenport 1990) reported leap "about 10 m s-1", glide up to 50 m, air speed 15 to 20 m s-1.
claims.note: Stall speed reproduces: analysis.py gives 9.854 m/s from 0.06 kg, 0.012688 m2 (= 6377+1837+4474 mm2 in the Table 1 row), CLmax 0.78, rho 1.225; it applies L3 body numbers to a different species.

claims.claim: Derived (lift = weight): a level lifting glide of 50 m at L/D 4.37 needs launch airspeed of at least 17.9 m/s (17.0 with a 14 percent ground-effect drag cut) given the stall floor; the bound holds only for lift = weight.
claims.source_says: analysis.py output: v0_needed_50m_noGE 17.9328, v0_needed_50m_GE14 17.0340; vmin 9.854. Check: 4.37*(v0^2-97.1)/(2*9.81)=50 gives v0=17.93. The 14% figure is from Park and Choi.
claims.note: I re-ran the script and the arithmetic reproduces; the scope caveat is stated honestly, and the cited evidence_quote is just the Park and Choi table row, not a source for this derivation.

overall: All four key claims hold. I read the Park and Choi, Deng and Makiguchi PDFs and re-ran analysis.py, and every number reproduces. The only soft spots are framing: 'only direct measurement' and 'underlies every bound' are judgments, and the stall speed applies model L3 numbers to other fish.
